rules.name: Mapping coyodex needs saying so
rules.statement: A run refuses to read or overwrite coyodex's own map unless the operator declares coyodex is the project being mapped.
rules.risk: A shell standing in the wrong folder reads a healthy result about the wrong product, or overwrites the accepted map.

sites.why: Refuses to read a map stored inside coyodex's own copy unless the run declared that coyodex is the project.
Refuses the same target for a write, so a stray build cannot overwrite the accepted map of coyodex.
Tells the build the refusal exists, and warns that a hand written script is not covered by the refusal.

rules.name: Git decides what is read
rules.statement: Only files git accounts for are analysed, so ignored and generated trees stay out of the map.
rules.risk: Reading everything on disk fills the map with built output and copied libraries, and hides the product's real size.

sites.why: Takes the starting file list from everything git tracks in the project.
Adds files someone created but never added yet, and leaves every ignored path to git.
Drops dependency folders, build output and caches by name, whether or not git is there to ask.

rules.name: Every exclusion is announced
rules.statement: A project's own exclusion patterns are named on every run, each beside the number of files it removed.
rules.risk: An over broad pattern hides a real gap from the very checks whose job is finding gaps.

sites.why: Names the patterns on every check run, including the cheap pass a lead runs most often.
Collects each pattern that removed nothing, so a typo cannot read as coverage the map never got.
Puts the same per pattern account in the briefing, printed before a build reads any code.

rules.name: Previous map stays closed
rules.statement: A build never opens the map it is replacing, so the new map cannot quietly copy the old one.
rules.risk: Two maps agree because one copied the other, and nobody can tell copying from real agreement.

sites.why: Bans opening the map being replaced, including the one version history still holds and one already filed away.
Warns when a copy of a map sits among the files that are about to be read as code.

rules.name: Rebuild only when asked
rules.statement: A map is built again from scratch only when the person asks, because a rebuild discards the accepted map.
rules.risk: A silent rebuild throws away every hand correction and the record of which code version the map described.

sites.why: Sends an existing map to a change report, and makes a fresh build need a spoken request and a confirmation.
Says a build writes a new map over any existing one, so nothing of the older map is kept.

rules.name: Corrections live at the source
rules.statement: A correction only lasts where the build reads from, because every file the build produces is written again from scratch.
rules.risk: A repair everybody believes landed quietly disappears, and the same work is done again months later.

sites.why: Warns that a correction made to the finished map disappears the next time the pieces are merged.
Refuses a removal aimed at one piece, because the pieces beside that one cannot be seen from there.
Applies the recorded assignments after every merge, which is what makes those assignments last.
States the split: what must survive a rebuild goes in the assignment file, never in the finished map.
Compares the committed readable copy with a freshly generated one, and reports any difference.
States that the readable copy is generated from the map and never edited by hand.

rules.name: Accepted warnings get written down
rules.statement: A warning the person decides to accept is silenced only by a note written under a heading the checks read.
rules.risk: A note nobody reads leaves the same warning arriving every run, so the real warnings get waved through.

sites.why: Refuses a heading no check reads, because a note filed under such a heading silences nothing.
Drops each file named by a recorded note out of the advisory the finish check would otherwise raise.
Names the heading the finish check reads, after twenty notes were filed where nothing could find them.

rules.name: Uncommitted code marks the pin
rules.statement: A map names the version of the code it describes. That name is marked when the code on disk was never committed.
rules.risk: Unmarked, the map claims a committed version it does not describe. Every later comparison then misses the edits already baked in.

sites.why: appends the mark to the version name when anything is uncommitted
asks version control what is uncommitted, ignoring the map's own folder
tells the agent to offer the choice, and to mark the pin only if the person declines to commit
